channel.title: the shyn daybook
channel.description: Entries from the making of shyn — a local-first memory for your Mac.

item.title: the far side has to speak
item.description: Every recorder asks permission once and then trusts itself forever. shyn asks the audio instead: nothing is kept unless voice arrives on the system channel — someone who is not you. Music does not qualify, a video does not, and neither do you thinking out loud. The cost is a room, which has no far side at all.

item.title: nothing phones home, except this
item.description: shyn shipped with the line “nothing phones home”. v0.5.0-alpha added anonymous crash and usage reporting, which made that false — and the cask still printed the old vow at the end of every install. What the egress design had to satisfy, the two ways “never content, never file paths” turned out to be untrue when we generated real crash payloads, the count of stale claims, and why we will not call a pre-checked box opt-in.

item.title: forgetting is a feature
item.description: Every memory product pitches total recall; the property that makes an archive of your days tolerable is that you can make it stop. shyn forgets three ways — scheduled (screen captures age out, meetings persist), deliberate (the forget tool hard-deletes by document, source, or time range), and constitutional (meeting audio destroyed on transcription). No trash cans, no soft deletes: a delete that costs nothing deletes nothing.

item.title: a model that never leaves the room
item.description: shyn's capture is local and its index is local. Close the loop with a local model over MCP — Qwen3 on MLX, Open WebUI, mcpo — and your memory works with the wifi off. Honest findings: retrieval is identical everywhere; small models are fine clerks and poor librarians; /no_think; name the tool; size for tool use.

item.title: the audio is purged the moment the words land
item.description: How shyn remembers meetings without a bot in the room: on-device call detection with voice verification, local recording behind a pulsing red dot, Whisper transcription on your own silicon — and the audio deleted the moment the speaker-labeled transcript lands. Words in, bytes gone.

item.title: counts, never content
item.description: A design rule for memory tools: every surface that isn't the search result itself — popover, stats, logs, diagnostics, marketing — shows counts, health, and versions. Never anything you read, said, or wrote. Inconvenient roughly weekly, and worth it.

item.title: why shyn exists
item.description: Your AI is brilliant and amnesiac. Your life happens on your Mac all day and lands nowhere. What shyn captures (screen, meetings, browsing, notes), how it recalls (hybrid search over an encrypted local index), where the AI comes in (MCP, any client, even fully local models), and what it refuses to do (telemetry, content in the UI, anything cloud).

item.title: shyn caught us staging its own demo
item.description: We built a fictional person, Maya Chen, so our screenshots wouldn't expose a real person's memory. Then we asked our AI a question with the real shyn still connected — and it called the demo data fabricated. The most honest QA report we never wrote, and a tour of what shyn actually does.
